Help & about this tab

Each set is one sample column. A row (feature) belongs to a set if that cell passes the presence rule above. Three linked views (see UpSet.js components) use UpSet.js (AGPL-3.0). Each chart’s Pop out button (next to its title in the main panel) opens popout/upset_popout.html via postMessage (needed for file://); allow pop-ups. The Heatmap tab uses the same pattern with the shared popout/plot_popout.html. Plot toolbar PNG/SVG/dump/VEGA stay on the default UpSet.js controls.

Many sets selected: the Venn / Euler and Karnaugh views can become crowded. Consider comparing fewer columns for readability.

Hover a region in any view to highlight the same intersection in the others (linked selection).

UpSet

Venn diagram

Karnaugh map

More than 3 sets selected and the online area-proportional fitter (Eunoia) could not be loaded — overlap regions cannot be placed proportionally in that case, so only the circles (sized by feature count) are drawn. Use the Linked views UpSet plot for exact multi-set intersections. (≤ 3 sets always work offline.)

Proportional Venn

Notes & attribution

Circle areas are proportional to each set's feature count; the overlap between two circles is placed to match the intersection count (exact for 2 sets, approximate for 3). For 4+ sets the whole layout is fitted area-proportionally by the Eunoia library loaded from a CDN (falls back to sized circles when offline). The Shape dropdown above picks the shape family used by the fitter — Auto (circles for 1–3 sets, ellipses for 4+), Circle, Ellipse, Square, or Rectangle: with an explicit shape, 1–3 sets are fitted by Eunoia too (or the built-in solver if the CDN is unreachable), and a single selected set draws that shape directly. The Color theme dropdown changes the set/region palette. Hover a shape or region for the exact numbers.

Multi-set layout fitted with Eunoia (J. Larsson, github.com/jolars/eunoia, MIT OR Apache-2.0) — Larsson & Gustafsson (2018), Fitting area-proportional Euler diagrams, Set Visual. Reasoning 2018, CEUR-2116.

About Hybrid Differential

Combines a presence/absence test (exact binomial for single-feature groups, parametric bootstrap for multi-peptide groups) with an intensity test (limma moderated t / Welch) into one feature list at a single overall FDR. Excels for one-state proteins — observed in one group, absent in the other — where intensity alone has no contrast.

  • Use when missingness itself is informative (MNAR), or vs. plain Differential for presence-driven hits
  • Input is the current Nebula matrix + meta table; pick any meta column with n ≥ 2 per group

Wang et al. (2012) Bioinformatics 28:1586–1591. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bts193

Nothing analyzed yet

The Hybrid Differential test (Wang et al. 2012) merges two views of the same matrix: Stage I — presence/absence (exact binomial for single-feature groups; bootstrap for multi-peptide groups) and Stage II — intensity (log₂, optional median centering / min−1.5·IQR imputation, limma moderated t or Welch). Stage III builds one list at a single hybrid FDR Σ w·[cp+(1−cp)F_bin]/ #selected. It is the complement to plain Differential: use it when detection itself is differential (one-state proteins).

01Load & preprocess in Data Preparation → Data PreProcess (matrix + meta; Nebula is the sole data source).
02In the left sidebar, pick Group by + Group A / B (needs n ≥ 2 per group) and tune Target FDR / test.
03Click Run hybrid analysis — Feature table, Dataset, Analysis, Volcano, Hybrid scatter and Diagnostics appear.
How to read: H = hybrid (primary) list · B = presence/absence list · I = intensity list (all at same cp*); pep = per-feature posterior, fdr = list-level at min p. One-state badge = observed in one group only (paper's flagship case).
Reference: Wang et al. Bioinformatics 28(12):1586–1591 (2012) · doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bts193.

2

Stage I — presence/absence

paper §2.3–2.5

Per feature group, presence counts in the two groups are tested for differential presence (exact binomial for single-feature groups; parametric bootstrap for multi-feature groups), and an FDR curve is estimated from the mixture of null and alternative.

Fig.2 p-hist
3

Stage II — intensity

Storey–Tibshirani FDR

Quantities are log₂-transformed, (optionally) median-centered, left-censored small values are imputed, and a Welch t-test per feature group yields p-values; π₀ and the FDR curve follow Storey & Tibshirani (2003).

4

Stage III — hybrid selection

paper §2.6 · single overall FDR

The two stages are combined into one selection rule with a single false-discovery-rate estimate (hybrid FDR ≥ component FDRs by construction). Selected features are the union of the two component selections at their operating cutoffs.

D

Diagnostics & method notes

self-tests + deviations

Method (as in the paper, hybrid2 port)

For two comparison groups with n1, n2 samples, a feature is “present” when observed (>0). Stage I: exact binomial for single-feature groups, parametric bootstrap (structured/unstructured) for multi-feature groups. Stage II (hybrid2): log₂ → optional per-sample median centering (off by default, assumes null majority) → optional left-censored imputation at min −1.5·IQR (off by default: complete case, one-state features get pInt=— and are covered by Stage I) → by default limma moderated t (empirical-Bayes, prior df₀,s²₀ via fitFDist, borrowed across features, fractional df via regIncBeta; Welch selectable). Stage III: weighted hybrid FDR Σ w·[cp+(1−cp)F_bin]/ #selected, one list. Table adds pep (local posterior L₀/(L₀+L₁), flat 50/50) and fdr (global list-level FDR at min p, Fig.1 axis, capped at 1).

Deviations (hybrid2)

Intensity: log₂ + (optional median centering, off) + (optional imputation min−1.5·IQR, off) + limma moderated t (default, verified vs R limma 3.58.1 to 1e-12) or Welch; Storey–Tibshirani π₀ (quadratic fit to π₀(λ) extrapolated to λ→1). Exact exactTails now cumulative (bugfix), digamma/trigamma for limma prior, per-feature stdev.unscaled uses observed n, explicit 0/NA handling. Bootstrap weight f₀/f₁ adaptive window δ=0.01 doubled if empty, 2-sided |T*|. See hybrid2 README.

Notes

Input data are assumed pre-filtered (contaminants/decoys removed). Two groups are required; choose any two levels of the meta column. Features with no observations in either group contribute no signal.
